title: Hybrid routing: SLA vs cost tradeoffs — sensitivity analysis
content:
Purpose:
Run a compact sensitivity analysis to inform a hybrid routing policy that balances SLA commitments (latency/availability) with unit cost savings from using spot/cheaper regions and fallback tiers. This is an internal working doc — numbers are coarse and meant to guide experiments and policy thresholds.

Background / motivation:
- Product wants to offer two SLA tiers: Gold (p99 latency target <= 200ms, 99.9% availability) and Silver (p95 target <= 300ms, 99% availability).
- Using cheaper capacity (spot GPUs, lower-cost regions) can reduce per-token spend but increases risk of preemptions, occasional latency spikes, and cross-region network egress.
- Goal: define routing heuristics and guardrails so we can safely route varying fractions of Silver and low-priority Gold traffic to cost-optimized capacity while meeting SLAs for the rest.

Assumptions (baseline for models):
- Baseline workload: 1M requests/day, avg 120 tokens generated per request (output-only), token billing unit = per-1k-output tokens.
- On-demand GPU cost (per 1k tokens processed): $0.16 (includes infra + amortized infra ops).
- Spot GPU effective cost (if not preempted): $0.06 per 1k tokens (approx 0.375x on-demand).
- Spot preemption rate assumptions: low: 1.5%, med: 4.0%, high: 9.0% (varies by region and time).
- Preemption penalty: when a request lands on a spot VM and is preempted, we fallback to a warm on-demand instance; this results in additional latency for the affected request and 1.2x compute cost for that request (recompute + overhead).
- Cross-region egress/regional price delta: cheaper regions effective 0.85x base cost for compute but +$0.01 per 1k tokens egress penalty for cross-region routing in most configs.
- SLA impact from preemption: assume preemption causes that request to exceed latency SLO (counts as an error for availability).
- Cache/hot-path effect: 25% of prefixes hit a prefix cache; cached responses avoid full compute cost (apply 0.20x cost multiplier).

Model framing:
- Compute expected per-1k token cost for each routing bucket (on-demand-local, spot-local, on-demand-remote, spot-remote).
- Compute expected SLA violation rate (availability) as function of preemption and cross-region latencies.
- Run sensitivity sweeps over spot preemption rate and fraction of traffic routed to spot to find safe operating ranges.

Quick cost table (per 1M tokens processed ~ baseline request mix):
- On-demand-local (no cross-region): base cost = $160 (1M tokens -> 1000 * $0.16).
- Spot-local: base cost = $60, expected additional due to preemptions = preemption_rate * 0.2 * base_cost (approx extra 20% of a preempted request cost), net cost = base + penalty.
- On-demand-remote: compute cost = $136 (0.85x compute) + egress penalty $10 = $146.
- Spot-remote: compute cost = $51 + egress penalty $10 = $61, plus preemption penalty.

Example calculations (1M tokens/day simplified):
- Scenario A: 100% on-demand-local -> cost = $160, availability = baseline (~99.995%), latency p99 comfortably <200ms.

- Scenario B: 60% spot-local, 40% on-demand-local, spot preemption=4%:
  * Spot compute = 0.6 * $60 = $36
  * Preempt penalty (assume 1.2x cost for preempted portion): extra = 0.6 * 0.04 * 0.2 * $60 = $0.288 (approx) -> negligible at this scale but measurable over months
  * On-demand portion = 0.4 * $160 = $64
  * Total expected daily cost = $100.3 -> ~37% savings vs all on-demand.
  * Expected availability hit: 0.6 * 0.04 = 2.4% of requests see a preemption event that likely violates p99 for those requests. If Gold traffic is mixed in, unacceptable. But if Silver-only, might be acceptable depending on SLO definitions.

- Scenario C: 80% spot-remote, 20% on-demand-local, spot preemption=1.5%:
  * Spot-remote compute = 0.8 * $61 = $48.8
  * On-demand-local = 0.2 * $160 = $32
  * Preempt penalty extra approx = 0.8 * 0.015 * 0.2 * $61 = $0.146
  * Total = ~$81 -> 49% savings vs all on-demand but cross-region egress risk and p99 latency risk for user-visible traffic.

Interpretation / rules of thumb from sensitivity sweep:
- For Gold SLA (p99 <=200ms, 99.9% availability): route at most 0% of Gold traffic to spot-local with preemption >1% unless we provide immediate warm-on-demand fallback for the entire request path (i.e., synchronous fallback guarantees). In practice, keep Gold on reserved/on-demand pools or use a separate warm buffer (dedicated capacity).
- For Silver / BestEffort: routing 50–80% to spot-local at preemption <=4% gives substantial cost savings while keeping perceived latency acceptable in most traffic mixes, provided we accept 1–3% of requests that exceed p99 and those are non-critical.
- Cross-region routing can be cost-effective when compute delta > 20% (i.e., remote compute <=0.8x local) AND egress penalty < savings. Our threshold: only route to remote regions when compute_multiplier * (1 - cache_hit_rate) - egress_per_1k > 0.12 (12 cents per 1k tokens) — plug-in numbers from run.

Operational guardrails to implement in policy layer:
- Tagging: requests must carry SLA_tier tag (gold | silver | bulk) and region_constraints (patient | latency-sensitive).
- Circuit breaker on spot: if observed preemption rate in last 5m > 6% or p95 latency for spot pool rises > 2x baseline, throttle spot traffic down by 30% and spill to on-demand pools.
- Proactive warming: maintain a small pool of warm on-demand instances per customer for Gold traffic to allow instant failover without significant retry cost. Cost of warm pool per customer is small compared to SLA breach risk.
- Fractional rollout knobs: ability to gradually increase % routed to spot by customer, with automatic rollback if SLOs deviate beyond threshold.
- Per-route cost-saver score: compute expected savings per route = baseline_cost - expected_mixed_cost; routes below $X/month savings should not be complicated with hybrid routing unless customer requests.

Suggested policy prototypes (pseudocode):
- Policy gold: if SLA==gold -> route priority: on-demand-local > on-demand-remote (if local saturated and latency constraint allows) ; do not route to spot unless explicit customer opt-in.
- Policy silver: if SLA==silver and spot_preempt_rate(region) < 4% -> allow up to 70% to spot-local, remaining spill on-demand-local. Monitor p99 and availability; auto-throttle if p99_exceeds_threshold or preempt_rate spikes.
- Policy bulk (cron, queued inference): route to spot-remote aggressively (90%+) with best-effort fallback and asynchronous retry logic.

Experiment plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week 1: Implement metric collection dashboards for per-pool preempt_rate, per-pool p95/p99, per-customer fallback counts. Add labels for region and spot-vs-on-demand.
- Week 2: Run synthetic traffic replay (representative prompts) against a test customer routing to 100% spot-local with adjustable preemption injection (1%, 4%, 8%). Verify latency distribution and compute overhead.
- Week 3–4: Canary: pick 3 non-critical customers (consent) and route 25% of Silver traffic to spot-local in a staged ramp. Monitor SLA and user complaints.
- Week 5: If stable, increase to 50% for those customers, continue monitoring. If any breach, rollback and increase warm buffer.
- Week 6: Consolidate results and produce final recommended default knobs for the runtime and Console UI (percent slider defaults, preempt thresholds, visibility in Console).

Open questions / risks:
- How correlated are preemptions across AZ/region? If correlated, our fallback pool sizing needs to assume bursts not independent Bernoulli events.
- Do certain prompt types (longer sequences, LLMs with large KV cache) show worse preemption penalty due to warm-up costs? Need per-model profiles.
- Cost model sensitivity to token length distribution: many short responses amplify RPC overhead whereas long responses amplify compute cost; routing needs to consider request-level expected compute cost, not just token counts.
- How to surface costs and tradeoffs in Console so customers can choose opt-in per-route? UX follow-up needed.

Quick recommendations (actionable):
1) Default: Gold -> 0% spot; Silver -> default 30% spot-local with conservative circuit-breaker (6% preempt, p95>2x baseline); Bulk -> 90% spot-remote.
2) Implement per-pool preempt_rate metric and 5-minute rolling alert to runtime that triggers auto-throttle.
3) Add per-customer warm buffer config in Console (optional setting) and show estimated monthly cost vs expected savings.
4) Start canary on 3 consenting customers (Silver) at 25% spot allocation.

Notes to reviewers:
- Numbers are intentionally simplified; before shipping any default customers-facing knob we should run the synthetic replay to recompute exact per-1k token deltas.
- I left small margins (e.g., 0.2x extra compute for preempted requests) — we should replace these with instrumented measurements from the spot fallback codepath.

Links / references:
- JIRA: INF-2345 (routing hybrid policy experimental tracking)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/678

If we accept this direction I can produce a companion sheet with per-model coefficients and an exportable CSV that the Console team can use to power the slider cost preview.
